title: Torque: The Twist That Makes Things Turn
hook: Why is a long wrench easier than a short one? Torque is rotational force — it grows with how far from the pivot you push, not just how hard.
key_points: Torque is the turning effect of a force — the rotational counterpart of a straight-line push.
It equals the force times the lever-arm distance from the pivot.
Push farther from the hinge and the same force produces more turning.
A door handle sits far from the hinges for exactly this reason.
content_html: Torque is what force becomes when you want something to spin instead of slide. Push on a door, tighten a bolt, or pedal a bike, and what matters isn't just how hard you push but how far from the pivot your push lands. That distance is the lever arm, and torque is the force multiplied by it.
extra_html: This is why tools and everyday objects are shaped the way they are. A long wrench, a door handle set far from the hinges, a bike crank — each gives you a generous lever arm so a modest force creates a strong twist. Push closer to the pivot and you have to push much harder for the same effect. Wikipedia lays out the precise definition and how torque relates to rotation, the angular cousin of Newton's straight-line laws.

flashcards.prompt: What two things does torque depend on?
flashcards.back_html: The force applied and the lever-arm distance from the pivot to where the force acts. More distance means more turning for the same force.

flashcards.prompt: Why is it easier to loosen a stiff bolt with a longer wrench?

choices.text: The longer arm increases torque for the same force you apply
A longer wrench is heavier, so gravity helps
Longer metal is stronger and bends the bolt directly

flashcards.explanation_html: Torque is force times lever-arm distance. A longer wrench moves your hand farther from the bolt, multiplying the turning effect of the same push.

flashcards.prompt: Where are door handles usually placed, and why?

choices.text: Far from the hinges, to maximize the lever arm and turning effect
Near the hinges, so less of the door has to move
In the center, to balance the force evenly

flashcards.explanation_html: Placing the handle far from the hinges gives a long lever arm, so a gentle push produces enough torque to swing the door.
